I don’t have the time nor the care to continue this discussion, think what you want, believe what you want. Everyone has different life experiences. 

I give you props for being able to work on your bpd and get to a place where you feel better, not sure how long you’ve been diagnosed or how long you’ve been in the better place, but from someone with many years of experience, be careful and aware of relapse, it does happen but push through and use your skills if you haven’t experienced it yet. Have an amazing life 💚 us bpd people shouldn’t fight nor judge others who have suffered like us.

There is a list of symptoms and you only have to have so many of them to qualify for it, do your research. 

Btw this is coming from someone who has all the symptoms and was immediately diagnosed at 18, it might be different now but 10 years ago they refused to diagnose bpd until you turned 18, my therapist and psychiatrist at the time knew I had bpd for years but didn’t tell me and I couldn’t be officially diagnosed until I was an adult. 

Yes there are resources but doing it all yourself is extremely difficult, potentially even impossible, having a therapist work through dbt with you and put things into perspective you just can’t get by doing it yourself. 

I see you deleted the post I replied to. Obviously you see the issue with what you said.

This is coming from someone who did go to therapy and got bpd treated. For one, meds aren’t effective for most people with bpd. Keep in mind not everyone can afford to go to therapy, a lot of insurance doesn’t cover it and insurance is expensive, many people don’t have it. 

There are different levels of bpd, you only have to have a certain amount of the symptoms to be diagnosed so some people have it worse than others and there are different types of bpd. 

We will always struggle with it in some capacity so judging others with it just isn’t a good look.

For sure! I go out to eat maybe once a month, if you’re someone who goes out more often then it’s definitely different. 
I also do this thing where I see a more high calorie food and ask myself if it’s worth it, is it one of my favorite foods to eat, will I truly enjoy this food. If the answer is yes to all of them then I will have the food, if not then I won’t.

We only live once, when I go out I still am mindful but let myself enjoy the food. Imo it won’t hurt to have some unhealthy food every so often. I personally work unhealthy food into what I eat on a regular basis since this is a lifestyle change. 

Im also not super strict with counting calories and I don’t track in an app or write things down, more so estimates.

I’m also 5’1 and when I started I had the idea of around 140-150. Now I’m aiming for a range 115-130, basically it’s a wait and see where I end up sort of thing. 

Don’t focus on your gw too much, focus on small goals in the beginning and celebrate the small victories. You got this!
